hook: A visible-light ring expansion in acridine compounds stores solar energy for up to 1.4 years
summary: Molecular solar thermal compounds store sunlight in strained bonds and release it later as heat. These acridine N-oxides absorb blue light at 470 nm, convert to a metastable form, and hold the energy up to 1.4 years in the solid state. Energy density, up to 0.54 MJ/kg, is modest, and the work is on small-molecule chemistry, not devices.
title: Visible-Light-Driven Dearomatization via Electrocyclic Ring Expansion for Solar Energy Storage
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
